questions.question: Which famous landmark is this?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty was a present to the United States from France, unveiled in 1886.

questions.question: In which city is this famous building?
questions.explanation: The Sydney Opera House's roof is covered in more than a million tiles.

media.alt: A famous building by the water
media.credit: Photo: Bernard Spragg. NZ from Christchurch, New Zealand, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: What is the official name of the London clock tower that holds the bell called Big Ben?
questions.explanation: It was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for the Queen's Diamond Jubilee; Big Ben is the great bell inside.

questions.question: In which country would you find the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
questions.explanation: The tower started to lean while it was still being built, more than 800 years ago.

questions.question: Which famous landmark is this?
questions.explanation: All the sections of the Great Wall added together stretch for more than 20,000 kilometres.

questions.question: This building, carved into a cliff, is in which ancient city?
questions.explanation: Petra, in Jordan, was carved straight into rose-red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans.

media.alt: A building carved into a rock face

questions.question: The Alhambra palace is in which Spanish city?
questions.explanation: Most of the Alhambra was built by the Nasrid rulers of Granada in the 13th and 14th centuries.

questions.question: Which Paris landmark was built as the entrance arch to the 1889 World's Fair?
questions.explanation: It was only meant to stand for 20 years.

questions.question: In which country is this temple?
questions.explanation: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world, and it appears on Cambodia's flag.

media.credit: Photo: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: The statue of Christ the Redeemer looks out over which city?
questions.explanation: The statue stands on top of Corcovado mountain and was finished in 1931.
